title: Electroporation-Mediated Delivery of Cas9 Ribonucleoproteins and mRNA into Freshly Isolated Primary Mouse Hepatocytes
protocol: Prepare Perfusion Solution 1 (HEPES, EGTA, and EBSS), Perfusion Solution 2 (HEPES, EGTA, EBSS, CaCl2, and MgSO4), and Perfusion Solution 3 (Solution 2 and Liberase).
Ensure the solutions are well mixed.
Set the water bath to 42 °C and prewarm Perfusion Solutions 1, 2, and 3 for a minimum of 30 min before starting the procedure.
Keep Perfusion Solutions in the water bath.
Place 150 mL of DMEM + 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in conical tubes and keep them on ice.
Sterilize pump tubing by placing both ends in a flask filled with 70% ethanol and cycling three times.
Wash tubing with distilled water and empty it.
Fill the tubing with prewarmed 30 mL of Perfusion Solution 1.
Follow by filling the tubing with 8 mL of Perfusion Solution 2.
If space remains in the tubing, fill it with Perfusion Solution 3.
Stop the pump when switching to a different perfusion solution.
Place excess tubing into a 42 °C water bath to keep solutions warm.
Place the end of the pump tubing in a conical tube containing Perfusion Solution 3 kept in the water bath.
Anesthetize the mouse by injecting anesthetic cocktail intraperitoneally at a dose of 10-11.7 µL/g body weight.
Monitor the breathing rate and check for pain response.
Wait until the breathing rate is ~55-65 breaths per minute, the mouse does not react to having its toes pinched, and the tail is flaccid.
Check the palpebral reflex by lightly touching the skin on the medial side of the closed eye.
Increase the dose of the entire anesthetic cocktail by 5-10 µL if the mouse blinks or twitches in response to touch.
Place the mouse on its back in a supine position.
Secure the limbs to the surface using pins or tape.
Spray the abdomen with 70% ethanol.
Pat the abdomen dry using a cotton ball.
Make a U-shaped lateral incision in the abdomen skin using scissors.
Cut through the peritoneum to expose the abdominal cavity up to the rib cage.
Move the intestines to the right side using the back of forceps or the blunt surface of scissors.
Identify the inferior vena cava and the portal vein.
Start the pump to flush prewarmed perfusion solution through the catheter.
Remove the needle from the catheter once all air has been flushed through the system.
Insert the tip of the needle connected to the catheter into the inferior vena cava at a 10°-20° angle.
Gently push the catheter into the vein in a movement parallel to the vein.
Observe flashback of blood in the catheter to verify proper cannulation in the vein.
Connect the tubing to the catheter without moving it further into the vein.
Start the pump with a 2 mL/min flow rate.
Look for the liver turning pale as a sign that perfusion is successful.
Cut the portal vein using scissors.
Gradually increase the flow rate to 5 mL/min.
Apply pressure periodically to the portal vein at the approximate cut site for 3 seconds using forceps or a cotton swab to block drainage and facilitate good perfusion.
Monitor the elasticity of the liver once Perfusion Solution 3 is flowing through.
Gently press the liver with a cotton swab or forceps to check if indentations form, indicating softness.
Stop the pump and remove the catheter when the liver is softened after 30-50 mL of Perfusion Solution 3 has flowed through.
Dissect the liver carefully and place it into a 100 mm Petri dish containing ice-cold DMEM + 10% FBS medium.
Excise the gallbladder without spilling its contents.
Swirl the Petri dish gently to remove possible blood clots.
Transfer the liver to a new Petri dish containing ice-cold DMEM + 10% FBS medium.
Place the Petri dish on ice and use two pairs of sterile forceps to gently tear apart the liver capsule on all lobes.
Gently swirl the liver in the medium using a cell lifter or forceps to release hepatocytes.
Continue swirling until the liver becomes very small and the suspension turns brown and opaque.
Remove liver tissue from the plate.
Transfer cell suspension using a 25 mL serological pipette fitted with a 100 μm cell strainer into a prechilled 50 mL conical tube.
Add fresh, ice-cold DMEM + 10% FBS medium to wash and collect remaining cells from the Petri dish surface.
Transfer washed cells to the 50 mL conical tube.
Repeat washing step until all cells are collected.
Centrifuge the cell suspension in the 50 mL conical tube at 50 × g at 4 °C for 5 min at low deceleration or without any brakes.
Discard supernatant containing debris and nonparenchymal cells.
Resuspend pellet gently by swirling the tube with leftover supernatant.
Add 30 ml of fresh, ice-cold DMEM + 10% FBS medium to resuspended pellet.
Repeat centrifugation and washing three times.
Resuspend final cell pellet in 10 ml of ice-cold DMEM + 10% FBS medium based on pellet size.
Prepare a 1:5 dilution by adding 50 μl of 0.4% Trypan Blue solution to 350 μl of Hepatocyte Plating Medium (PM).
Add 100 μl of cell suspension into the mixture and pipette up and down multiple times to mix thoroughly.
Count cell density and viability using a hemocytometer.
Place the hepatocyte suspension on ice while counting.
Place the ice bucket containing the suspension on an orbital shaker set to 30 rpm.
Follow Percoll treatment and centrifugation if cell viability is less than 70%.
Dilute Percoll with 10x phosphate-buffered saline in a 9:1 ratio.
Mix hepatocyte suspension with diluted Percoll in a 1:1 ratio.
Centrifuge at 200 × g at 4 °C for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant containing dead cells.
Resuspend the pellet in ice-cold DMEM + 10% FBS medium.
Count the cells again.
Plate some of the cells on collagen I-coated 6-well plates at a density of 0.5 × 10^6 cells per mL using 1.5 mL of prewarmed PM.
Keep remaining cells on ice while on an orbital shaker until ready for electroporation.
Place the plate of cells in a water-jacketed CO2 incubator at 37 °C.
Move the plate horizontally and vertically gently to ensure homogeneous plating, repeating every 1.5 h.
Verify cell attachment at 3 hours after plating.
Change the medium to prewarmed Hepatocyte Maintenance Medium (MM) at 24 hours post-plating to maintain cells in culture.
Remove the spent medium from the cultured cells after cell attachment to the 6-well collagen I-coated plates.
Fix the cells for 10-15 minutes in ice-cold ethanol.
Wash thoroughly with sterile water.
Incubate in 1% aqueous periodic acid for 5 minutes.
Wash with sterile water.
Incubate in 100% Schiff Reagent for 30 minutes.
Wash with water three times over 10 minutes.
Mount in mounting medium.
Image using a microscope on brightfield setting.
Add the entire accompanying supplement to the PM and warm in the 37 °C water bath for 10 min.
Turn on the electroporation device by pressing the power button.
Set the electroporation program by pressing the x button and then the down arrow button until the program T-028 appears on the screen.
Prepare the destination wells for the electroporated hepatocytes by adding 1.5 mL of PM to six-well collagen I-coated plates.
Incubate the plates in a 37 °C incubator until ready to use.
Add the entire accompanying supplement to the electroporation buffer solution and incubate at room temperature for 10 min.
Label the electroporation buffer expiration date on the vial (3 months after the date of supplement addition).
Remove the electroporation vessels from the packaging.
Label them for each sample.
Prepare Cas9 RNP complexes by combining 30 µg of sgRNA with 300 pmol of Cas9 protein.
Incubate the Cas9 RNP complexes at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Prepare Cas9 mRNA by mixing 30 µg of sgRNA with 4 µL of Cas9 mRNA (1 µg/µL).
Store the mRNA-sgRNA mix on ice until electroporation.
Centrifuge 1.2 × 10^6 cells per electroporation reaction at 100 × g for 2 minutes at 4 °C.
Remove the supernatant from the cell pellet and add 100 µL of electroporation solution along the side of the tube wall.
Resuspend the hepatocytes in the electroporation solution by gently rocking the tube by hand.
Add 1.0 µg of eGFP mRNA to a separate tube for fluorescence microscopy verification.
Transfer 100 µL of the hepatocyte suspension using wide-bore pipette tips to the strip tubes containing Cas9 complexes.
Place the nucleovette vessel into the electroporation device slot.
Electroporate the hepatocytes by pressing the x button on the device.
Wait for the screen to indicate "OK" after electroporation.
Press the x button again and remove the vessel from the device.
Incubate the electroporated vessel on ice for 15 minutes.
Add 500 µL of prewarmed PM to the electroporation vessel.
Transfer 300 µL of the electroporation reaction to each destination well on the prewarmed plate.
Disperse cells by gently moving plates horizontally and vertically in a north-to-south and east-to-west motion at 15, 30, 45, 60, and 90 min after plating.
Incubate the plates overnight at 37 °C.
Remove the medium from the wells designated for gene editing analysis 24 h after plating the cells.
Replace with 0.25 mg/mL basement membrane matrix overlay.
Thaw the membrane matrix if stored in the freezer and transfer to 4 °C.
Calculate the volume of the membrane matrix needed to mix with MM to give a final concentration of 0.25 mg/mL for each well.
Add the calculated volume of the membrane matrix to ice cold MM.
Mix by pipetting up and down 10 times.
Pipette the overlay mixture slowly on top of the cells.
Place the plate back in the 37 °C incubator.
Replace the medium with fresh maintenance medium every 24 h.
Transfer the conditioned medium from the well designated for MTT and albumin assays at 24 h after plating.
Store the conditioned medium in a microfuge tube until ready to perform the albumin assay.
Proceed to step 7.1 for the MTT assay.
Prepare 12 mM MTT stock solution by adding 1 mL of PBS to one 5 mg vial of MTT.
Add 150 µL of the MTT stock solution to the wells and incubate for 24 h.
After incubation, add 1.5 mL of sodium dodecyl sulfate-hydrochloride (SDS-HCl) solution to each well.
Pipette to mix the solution in each well thoroughly.
Incubate the plate for 4 h at 37 °C and observe a change in medium color from clear to purple, indicating viable cells.
Mix each sample again using a pipette.
Read the absorbance at 570 nm using a microplate reader.
Transfer 50 µL of conditioned medium to the wells in the plate provided by the albumin kit.
Cover the wells and incubate for 2 h at room temperature.
Wash the wells 5x with 200 µL of wash buffer.
Invert the plate to empty each well on tissue paper and tap a few times.
Add 50 µL of the biotinylated antibody provided in the albumin assay kit to each well and incubate at room temperature for 1 h.
Repeat steps to wash the wells with wash buffer.
Add 50 µL of streptavidin-peroxidase provided in the albumin assay kit to each well and incubate at room temperature for 30 min.
Repeat step to wash the wells with wash buffer.
Add 50 µL of the chromogen substrate provided in the albumin assay kit per well and incubate for 30 min at room temperature.
Gently tap the plate to ensure even mixing.
Remove any air bubbles with a pipette tip.
Lastly, add 50 µL of stop solution to each well.
Look for a color change from yellow to blue to indicate functional cells.
Proceed immediately to read the absorbance at 450 nm using a microplate reader.
Estimate the delivery efficiency in wells electroporated with eGFP mRNA.
Capture phase contrast and green fluorescence images of hepatocytes 24 h after electroporation.
Take three images at different locations within the well.
Upload images of the cells to ImageJ.
Under the Image tab, select Type | 16-bit to convert image to greyscale.
To highlight cell structures in the image, under the Image tab, select Adjust | Threshold.
Adjust the slider to highlight cells.
Under the Process tab, select Subtract Background to remove background noise.
Count the cells by clicking the Analyze tab and then selecting Analyze particles.
Click Ok to generate a list of counted particles.

Calculate the percentage of GFP-positive cells by dividing the number of counted particles in the green fluorescence images by the number of counted particles in the corresponding phase contrast image.
Extract genomic DNA from electroporated cells.
Remove medium from the plate 3 days after electroporation, and add 500 μL of 0.25% trypsin.
Incubate at 37 °C for 5 min.
Pipette several times after incubation to ensure hepatocytes have detached from the plate.
Transfer the trypsinized cell suspension to microcentrifuge tubes and spin in a tabletop centrifuge at 800 × g for 10 min at room temperature.
Examine the tubes for pellets.
Remove the supernatant containing trypsin by pipetting, making sure not to disturb the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 80 µL of DNA extraction solution.
If the pellet is difficult to see, resuspend the content of the tube in 50 μL of DNA extraction solution.
Vortex for 30 s to ensure the pellet is resuspended.
Transfer the suspension to PCR split-strip tubes and place them in the thermal cycler.
Run for 15 min at 95 °C and 8 min at 68 °C.
PCR-amplify the on-target locus.
Mix 0.5 µL of 10 mM dNTPs with the reaction components.
Add 0.5 µL of 10 µM Forward primer to the reaction mixture.
Add 0.5 µL of 10 µM Reverse primer to the reaction mixture.
Pipette 0.125 µL of Taq polymerase into the PCR mix.
Transfer 5 µL of genomic DNA extracted from hepatocytes into the tube.
Mix 18.375 µL of nuclease-free water with other components in the PCR mix.
Vortex the PCR mix briefly and quickly centrifuge to concentrate at the bottom.
Place the PCR mix in a thermal cycler for denaturation at 94 °C for 30 s.
Cycle through 30 cycles: Denature at 94 °C for 30 s, anneal at 57 °C for 45 s, extend at 68 °C for 1 min.
Perform a final extension step at 68 °C for 5 min.
Mix 3 µL of PCR products with 2 µL of water and 1 µL of 6x dye.
Run the mixture on a 1.5% agarose gel to confirm product size.
Purify DNA using magnetic beads after reaching room temperature from storage at 4 °C.
Vortex the PCR mix briefly and quickly centrifuge again before purification.
Add a volume of beads equal to 1.8× the volume of the PCR mix to the solution.
Mix the PCR-bead mix 10 times to ensure uniformity.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 10 min.
Transfer the PCR-bead mix to a PCR plate.
Place the PCR plate on a magnetic plate.
Incubate the plate on the magnet for 5 min.
Check that the solution is clear and beads are bound before proceeding.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 200 µL of 70% ethanol to the well.
Incubate for 30 s.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat step of adding 200 µL of 70% ethanol, incubating for 30 s, and discarding the supernatant.
Remove the plate from the magnet after drying for 3 min at room temperature to remove traces of ethanol.
Add 22 µL of water to the sample.
Pipette up and down 10x to mix water and beads.
Incubate the samples for 3 min at room temperature.
Transfer the plate back to the magnet and incubate for 3 min or until the solution is clear.
Transfer 20 µL of the sample to a PCR tube, taking care not to carry over any beads.
Sequence purified DNA amplicon by Sanger sequencing.
Upload .ab1 sequence files for treated and control samples to Tracking of Indels by Decomposition (TIDE) for quantification of indels at the target site.
